data.hypothesis: Interleaving the two terminal-power recurrences may reduce loop and SIMD-dispatch overhead while preserving each direction's multiplication order and all payoff indices. Whether this improves the full call remains to be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this program, a transformation slower in isolation may still contribute to a faster combination; judge integrations with whole-call controller measurements.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured T1+T4+T2+T3 integration was correct at 0.019241 s, compared with 0.037432 s for T1+T4; isolated T2 and T3 trials were slower than either integration.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this paired-loop variant against 600ed5dcd12b4666 for correctness and whole-call timing before retaining it.

data.notes: The parent 600ed5dcd12b4666 was measured correct at 0.019241 s. This proposal changes only terminal recurrence loop organization; it has not been evaluated or independently confirmed.
transformations: Based on the valid measured G source, retaining its lane-contiguous batches, thread-budget-aware outer parallelism, double-precision powers, and hoisted rollback coefficients.
Interleave positive- and negative-exponent recurrence updates in one lane-SIMD loop, retaining each direction's multiplication order and the full j=0..63 exponent mapping.
